title: How c Changes the Roots
prompt: Move the slider in $y = x^2 - 4x + c$ and watch how the parabola changes its intersections with the $x$-axis.

fallback.markdown: For $y = x^2 - 4x + c$, the discriminant is $16 - 4c$. When $c < 4$, the graph has two real $x$-intercepts. When $c = 4$, it touches the axis once at $x = 2$. When $c > 4$, it has no real $x$-intercepts.
